title: Działki nad Liwcem — wybierz świat wizualny
question: The roll assigned Targ — fluo price cards. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Targ — fluo price cards
options.lineage: hand-lettered fluorescent price cards on Polish market stalls
options.thesis: Price is the loudest thing on every row, and whatever changed since yesterday is shouted on fluorescent card.
options.viewport: Slim top bar with 'since your last visit' counts and filters; below, one dense sortable table of every plot, price figures set large in marker weight, NOWE / TANIEJ / ZNIKNĘŁO as fluo card tags.
options.risk: Marker lettering tips into gimmick if it spreads beyond price figures and state tags.

raised.raise: Prices and areas right-aligned in tabular figures tight to the column edge, read like a stall's price list.
One fluorescent accent owns every live state (new, cheaper); colour is never decoration.
Days on market encoded on one fixed fresh-to-stale ramp, identical everywhere.
Strict whole-cell grid: columns never shift, filters only hide rows.

options.label: Odjazdy — PKP timetable poster
options.lineage: the yellow 'Odjazdy' departure timetable on every Polish station wall
options.thesis: Plots set in the column rhythm of the yellow station timetable, grouped by day listed, footnote marks carrying state.
options.viewport: Yellow header band with 'Nowe od wczoraj: 9'; table grouped under day headings like departure hours, price and PLN/m² columns, footnote glyphs for price drops and gone listings.
options.risk: The most direct read of 'what is new', and the time-table metaphor many tools reach for.

options.label: Split-flap concourse board
options.thesis: Every plot a departure row; price drops flip amber, gone listings drop to dim red.
options.viewport: Black board of fixed-cell rows ranked by date listed, condensed caps, amber lamps on changed rows.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: rows ranked by time and delay/cancel states map to cheaper/gone; loses on your 'no gimmicks' — flap motion fights quick price reading.
options.risk: Black-board density on a laptop reads heavy for a few-minute daily check.

options.label: Convention circle catalog
options.thesis: A packed grid of compact plot cells; shortlisted ones circled in pen, seen ones struck through.
options.viewport: Edge-to-edge grid of small plot cells with code, village and price; pen-circled shortlist pinned on top.
options.case: Holds clarity: circled = shortlisted, struck = seen is instantly legible triage; you would not recognise the form itself.
options.risk: Cell grid compares prices worse than a table column does.

options.label: Mixtape j-card
options.thesis: Listings as a ruled tracklist, durations right-aligned.
options.viewport: Side A / Side B halves of a ruled list.
options.case: Loses both axes: no tie to land buying, halves split one list for no reason.
options.kept: Right-aligned figures tight to the margin.

options.label: Metro typographic tiles
options.thesis: Giant cropped lowercase over flat colour tiles.
options.viewport: Panorama of tiles, one plot per tile.
options.case: Loses both: exactly the 'too sparse' you ruled out.
options.kept: One accent owns every live state.

options.label: Star atlas
options.thesis: Plots as stars, magnitude as price.
options.viewport: A chart of dots you hover to read.
options.case: Loses both: hides prices behind a metaphor.
options.kept: One quantity on one fixed ramp.

options.label: Crouwel grid specimen
options.thesis: The grid itself as the visible armature.
options.viewport: Monumental numerals on a visible grid.
options.case: Loses both: a poster, not a daily tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean data-table app (Airtable / Linear list style), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Filter bar, sortable table, side panel with listing details.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other tool by design.
